text:
Mikhail Sergachev is playing like a No. 1 defenseman and getting paid in minutes for it: 26:08 a night over his last ten games, about three minutes above his norm, with 22 points through 21 games. Utah controls 57% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at five on five when he's out there, and that part looks real. The six goals are the bit to hold loosely. They come from 3.1 expected, on 11.5% shooting, well above what our numbers consider his true rate, so the scoring should drift back toward his usual playmaking.

The playmaking was always the point. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 94th percentile among defensemen in primary shot assists last season, and stopping 17% of the entries aimed at him against a typical 11%. Off the ice, his name sits inside another story. His old Tampa Bay teammate Nikita Kucherov, who won two Stanley Cups beside him, has asked for a trade; Sergachev told RG.org why he backs the request, and Bolavip reported Utah as a suitor with Sergachev's help. A rumor, for now, but one with his fingerprints on it.
